summary:
The Manitoba Human Rights Code prohibits discrimination on the basis of gender identity in employment, housing and accommodation. On 18 March 2025 the provincial government introduced a bill to add gender expression as a protected ground; Justice Minister Matt Wiebe stated the change would bring Manitoba into line with most other provinces and would cover preferred pronouns and outward appearance such as clothing. The bill was before the Legislative Assembly for debate later in 2025, and Trans Manitoba executive director Charlie Eau welcomed it.

Statistics Canada reported on 30 March 2026 that Manitoba recorded the joint-lowest provincial police-reported hate crime rate in 2024, at 5.3 per 100,000, alongside Newfoundland and Labrador, with no increase over 2023. The national rate was 12.1 per 100,000 across 4,882 reported hate crimes. These figures count only incidents reported to police.

The Legislative Assembly passed a bill on 30 May 2024 recognising 31 March as Two-Spirit and Transgender Day of Visibility, introduced by Logan Oxenham, an openly trans MLA for Kirkfield Park. On 20 November 2023 the province raised the transgender flag in Winnipeg's Memorial Park for the Transgender Day of Remembrance, an observance first marked eight years earlier, with ministers Nahanni Fontaine and Uzoma Asagwara issuing a statement of government support for trans, two-spirit and gender-diverse Manitobans.

Changing the gender marker on birth certificates and vital statistics documents falls under provincial jurisdiction in Canada; the specific Manitoba procedure is not documented in this record.
tangentialFactors:
Provincial hate-crime statistics for 2024 place Manitoba at the low end among Canadian provinces, but police-reported data capture only incidents that are reported and recorded as hate-motivated.

Other Canadian provinces have moved in a restrictive direction on trans rights, including Saskatchewan's 2023 parental-consent law for students' gender-related names and Alberta's 2024 and 2025 education, health and sport statutes, some insulated from court challenge by the notwithstanding clause. Manitoba's 2025 bill to add gender expression to its human rights code runs against that trend.
localsOnly:
Manitoba's Human Rights Code already prohibits discrimination based on gender identity; the pending amendment would extend the same protection to gender expression, including preferred pronouns and clothing.

Logan Oxenham, the first openly trans man elected to the Manitoba legislature, sponsored the bill recognising Two-Spirit and Transgender Day of Visibility, passed 30 May 2024.
outOfScopeNotes:
The specific Manitoba procedure and requirements for changing a gender marker on a birth certificate or other vital statistics document are not documented in this record.

Whether the 2025 gender-expression amendment has been enacted is unresolved in this record; the latest sourced status is a bill before the legislature scheduled for debate later in 2025.

No Manitoba-specific incident of violence against a trans person is documented in this record; the Brandon advocate's November 2023 statement that transphobic violence shows no sign of slowing is an undated-prevalence characterisation, not a counted figure.
